elements.element: Customer is not liable for liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Customer shall not be liable to Vendor for any liquidated damages.

elements.element: Customer is not liable for penalties.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Customer shall not be liable to Vendor for any penalties.

elements.element: Any liquidated amount payable by Customer may arise only from early termination.
elements.evidence: The clause categorically eliminates all liquidated amounts payable by Customer, so no liquidated amount can arise outside early termination.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Customer is expressly not liable for any liquidated damages or penalties, so no early-termination fee exceeding the cap is payable.

elements.element: No liquidated amount other than the permitted early-termination fee is payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The blanket prohibition on Customer liability for liquidated damages and penalties excludes every other liquidated amount.

result.reason: The operative language fully achieves the preferred position by eliminating all liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer. It also satisfies the fallback as a more protective result: no noncompliant early-termination fee or other liquidated amount can arise. The redline is not minimal because it additionally grants equitable extensions and makes them Vendor's sole remedy for dependency delay, neither of which is necessary to eliminate liquidated damages. Those additions remain related to the deleted delay remedy and do not contradict the prohibition or disturb unrelated commercial terms.
